text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Your mother is concerned about your attention issues and behavioral changes; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been happening and if they vary by setting (e.g., at school vs. at home)?

REQUEST TEST: Developmental_&_Behavioral_History_Review
REQUEST IMAGES: None needed at this time.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: The Developmental & Behavioral History Review indicates that the patient's attention issues and behavioral changes are consistent with her stated age and have been present intermittently since early adolescence. Symptoms appear to be more pronounced during high-stress periods and when discussing family dynamics (specifically regarding her mother), but she functions effectively in routine settings. There is no evidence of developmental delays or new-onset neurological symptoms. The patient reports a history of being labeled "daydreamy" in school but has always maintained good academic performance with minimal intervention.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood. The clinical picture of intermittent symptoms tied specifically to high-stress periods and family dynamics, without developmental delays or significant academic decline, is most consistent with an emotional reaction to a psychosocial stressor rather than a primary neurodevelopmental disorder.
